payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) affects gender bias in predictions and model performance, specifically through the process of gender-swapping and its impact on F1 scores.

claims.text: Counterfactual Data Augmentation (CDA) mitigates contextual gender biases by equalizing the contexts for masculine and feminine words in training data, leading to improved model performance.
Using CDA significantly decreases the F1 score gap between predictions on male and female sentences, thus improving fairness in model predictions.
CDA, when combined with other debiasing methods, enhances overall model performance while reducing gender bias in predictions.
